ROLE: Run a bounded burst of nonblocking reads into the session input buffer and hand the accumulated bytes to the protocol core after every successful read, turning would-block into a quiet return, dispatch EOF/error into the broker's EOF path, and closing only this session when its input cannot be buffered.

SIGNATURE.RAW: static void pump_read(struct loop *l, struct session *s)
SIGNATURE.NAME: pump_read

STRUCT.NAME: struct loop
STRUCT.ROLE: provides the borrowed broker that frames and answers packets

STRUCT.NAME: struct session
STRUCT.ROLE: owns the descriptor and the receive buffer that accumulates this burst

STRUCT.NAME: struct byte_buf
STRUCT.ROLE: growable receive buffer appended to by this function

FUNC.NAME: buffer_append
FUNC.ROLE: append the bytes just read to the receive buffer

FUNC.NAME: broker_process_input
FUNC.ROLE: frame, dispatch and consume every complete packet now buffered

FUNC.NAME: broker_session_eof
FUNC.ROLE: handle orderly close / read error: process complete frames, then finish after flushing

FUNC.NAME: session_close_immediately
FUNC.ROLE: close this session when its input cannot be buffered

VAR.NAME: LOOP_READ_CHUNK
VAR.ROLE: size of the stack staging chunk used for one read call (4096 bytes)

VAR.NAME: LOOP_MAX_READ_CALLS
VAR.ROLE: upper bound on read calls per descriptor per dispatched event (64)

VAR.NAME: NET_IO_PROGRESS
VAR.ROLE: a read transferred bytes; the out count says how many

VAR.NAME: NET_IO_WOULD_BLOCK
VAR.ROLE: no more bytes are available right now

VAR.NAME: NET_IO_CLOSED
VAR.ROLE: the peer performed an orderly close of its write side

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: session_fd
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: the descriptor owned by the session, or -1 when the session is NULL or already released its descriptor
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: borrowed descriptor number; the session keeps ownership and closes it exactly once later
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: no failure under documented preconditions; a negative result means the session is finished and the pump returns without a syscall

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: session_input
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: borrowed pointer to the receive buffer of the session (NULL only for a NULL session); the buffer keeps every unconsumed byte between calls and is emptied only by the protocol core's buffer_consume
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: borrowed; the session keeps the storage and frees it in session_destroy
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: no failure under documented preconditions; a NULL result is handled by closing the session

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: net_read_some
CALL_CONTRACTS.SIGNATURE: enum net_io_result net_read_some(int fd, uint8_t *buf, size_t cap, size_t *out_n)
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: NET_IO_PROGRESS with *out_n > 0 = bytes read into buf, NET_IO_WOULD_BLOCK = nothing available now, NET_IO_CLOSED = the peer closed and no byte was read, NET_IO_ERROR = failure; *out_n is set to 0 for anything but PROGRESS
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: the bytes are copied into the caller's staging chunk; the callee retains nothing, so the caller owns them from return and must copy them into the session buffer before discarding the chunk
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: WOULD_BLOCK is not an error; CLOSED and ERROR must be routed to broker_session_eof so that complete frames already buffered are still processed

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: buffer_append
CALL_CONTRACTS.SIGNATURE: int buffer_append(struct byte_buf *buf, const void *src, size_t len)
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: 0 after all len bytes were appended in order (len 0 is a successful no-op); -1 for a NULL buffer, a NULL source with len > 0, a size overflow or an allocation failure
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: the bytes are copied into buffer-owned storage; the source chunk stays valid but is not referenced afterwards
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: on -1 the buffer contents are unchanged, so no partial read is ever interpreted as a frame; the caller treats it as an unrecoverable per-connection failure and closes the session

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: broker_process_input
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: 0 when the session may continue, -1 when the session was closed by what it sent (malformed or unframeable packet, or a non-CONNECT packet before CONNECT); bytes of each handled packet are consumed from the receive buffer before returning
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: does not take ownership of the session; the session stays in the registry with state SESSION_CLOSED when it returns -1 and is destroyed later by broker_reap
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: -1 means the caller must stop pumping this descriptor: no further read may be issued for a session that is closing, and the mask synchronization will drop it

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: broker_session_eof
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: void; every complete packet already buffered is processed (so a final PUBLISH immediately followed by a half close is still routed), the trailing partial packet bytes are discarded, and the session enters SESSION_CLOSING with its queued output preserved for flushing
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: does not destroy the session or close its descriptor: the descriptor stays open until the queue drains and broker_reap runs, because the peer may still read the responses owed to it
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: no failure under documented preconditions; idempotent enough that a later read error on an already CLOSING session simply does not re-enter the input path

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: session_close_immediately
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: void; queued output is released, the descriptor is closed once and the state becomes SESSION_CLOSED (no-op when already CLOSED)
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: releases this session's descriptor and queue storage only; the session object stays registered until broker_reap destroys it
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: no failure under documented preconditions; the call is isolated to this session and never affects other clients

LOGIC.INPUT: l: the reactor (NULL tolerated). s: the session whose descriptor reported readability; the caller has already checked that s is still a registry entry and that its state is AWAITING_CONNECT or READY (EPOLLOUT alone never reaches this function).
LOGIC.ACTION: 1. If l == NULL or s == NULL or l->broker == NULL, return. 2. fd = session_fd(s); if fd < 0 return (the session already finished). 3. in = session_input(s); if in == NULL, session_close_immediately(s) and return. 4. For n = 0 to LOOP_MAX_READ_CALLS-1: r = net_read_some(fd, chunk, LOOP_READ_CHUNK, &got) where chunk is a LOOP_READ_CHUNK-byte stack array. 5. If r == NET_IO_WOULD_BLOCK, return: the burst is over and the level-triggered EPOLLIN event will fire again when more bytes arrive. 6. If r == NET_IO_CLOSED, call broker_session_eof(l->broker, s) and return: the peer shut down its write side, so any complete frames already buffered - including a PUBLISH that arrived immediately before the shutdown - are handled first and the session then finishes after flushing what it owes (scope R07/R08). 7. If r == NET_IO_ERROR, call broker_session_eof(l->broker, s) and return: a broken descriptor is treated the same way so buffered complete frames are still processed; the broken socket then fails the following write and the session is closed immediately by pump_write, so no session is stranded. 8. Otherwise r == NET_IO_PROGRESS and got > 0: if buffer_append(in, chunk, got) != 0, the bytes cannot be buffered (allocation failure); call session_close_immediately(s) and return, because failing to buffer input would corrupt framing if the bytes were dropped. 9. Call broker_process_input(l->broker, s); if it returns -1 the session closed itself (malformed or unframeable input, or a packet before CONNECT), so return without another read. 10. If got < LOOP_READ_CHUNK the kernel buffer was drained; return rather than issuing another read that would only return would-block. 11. Otherwise loop to the next read; the burst bound keeps a peer that streams without pause from monopolising the reactor, because the reactor returns after at most LOOP_MAX_READ_CALLS reads and serves every other ready descriptor, whose own responses are then written even though this peer is idle.
LOGIC.OUTPUT: void. Post-state: every byte read during the burst is either consumed as a complete packet by the protocol core or still buffered as a partial frame; the session is either still AWAITING_CONNECT/READY, CLOSING after an orderly close or a read error (with complete frames already handled), or CLOSED (its input could not be buffered, or its own input was rejected). Bytes consumed and bytes buffered always sum to the bytes read in this call, so no input is lost or duplicated.
INVARIANTS_USED: a session's own packets are framed with explicit Remaining Length counts, so partially received frames are preserved in the receive buffer for the next batch
bytes are consumed only for packets that were fully handled
the drain-after-close order is: process complete frames, then discard only the partial tail
read work per event is bounded so one peer cannot stall unrelated peers
a descriptor that is nonblocking is read only after a readable/hup/err readiness event
every failure path closes at most the session whose descriptor failed
LOGIC.PRECONDITION: s is a live registry entry in SESSION_AWAITING_CONNECT or SESSION_READY whose descriptor is nonblocking, close-on-exec and registered for EPOLLIN, and the dispatched event contained EPOLLIN, EPOLLRDHUP, EPOLLHUP or EPOLLERR.
LOGIC.POSTCONDITION: no read is issued for a session that is CLOSING or CLOSED, no byte is discarded except a partial frame after EOF, and the reactor state is consistent with the broker registry.
LOGIC.THREAD_SAFETY: Single-threaded reactor; the session is never touched concurrently.
